extra.message: The CredentialsProvider.authorize() callback authenticates users against a hard-coded username/password pair ('user'/'password'). These are publicly known default credentials, so any attacker can log in with them (trivially guessable, and brute-forcible since no rate limiting exists) and gain a valid session that passes the middleware/ProtectedRoute checks. Combined with the plaintext comparison, this is an authentication bypass via use of hard-coded credentials.

Sensitive secrets are hard-coded as literal JSX text on the dashboard page: an API key ('X92nJdsL8aQp03Mf'), a database connection string containing plaintext credentials ('mongodb://user:password@localhost:27017/db'), and a private server endpoint. Because this is a client-rendered Next.js page, these strings are compiled into the public /_next/static JS chunk, and the middleware matcher (middleware.js:47) explicitly excludes /_next/static from auth checks, so the secrets are exposed in source control and retrievable by any user who can obtain the chunk, not only authenticated sessions.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The next.config.js 'env' block exposes NEXTAUTH_SECRET (and NEXTAUTH_URL) as build-time environment variables. In Next.js, values declared in 'env' are inlined into the client-side JavaScript bundle, so the JWT signing secret is shipped to the browser. Anyone who can read the public bundle can obtain NEXTAUTH_SECRET and forge valid next-auth JWT session cookies, bypassing authentication on /dashboard, /profile, and /api/protected.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
